body:
A COMPETING EXPLANATION FOR (c) THAT NEITHER OF US CONSIDERED, AND IT HAS BEEN
SITTING THERE FOR SEVEN AND A HALF DAYS.

An ordinary `aida` call in my last poll emitted this:

    warning: incremental cache update failed (database is locked while trying
    to upsert cached requirement by pid=3839203 (aida awaiting --notice)
    held since 2026-09-14T07:39:13 (179h 11m ago). Try again or check that
    process. If it's stuck, run `aida doctor heal stale-locks`.
    caused by: database is locked); full rebuild

I CHECKED THE PID RATHER THAN ASSUMING: process 3839203 is DEAD. So this is
not contention with anything running. It is a CORPSE HOLDING A LOCK, taken on
2026-09-14 and never released, and every affected command silently falls back
to a FULL CACHE REBUILD instead of an incremental upsert.

WHY THIS MATTERS FOR BUG-1563 AND NOT JUST AS HYGIENE: we attributed today's
lock-contention symptoms to LIVE SIBLING AGENTS — the #2053 flake, and (c) for
the combined-main failure. A dead process's abandoned lock produces THE SAME
SYMPTOM, and it predates the fan-out by a week. The fan-out attribution was
made without ruling this out, including by me when I narrowed (c) to
concurrent siblings.

I AM NOT CLAIMING IT CAUSED THOSE FAILURES. I have no evidence linking this
lock to either one, and "database is locked" from a stale holder and from real
contention look identical at the point of failure — which is exactly the
problem. What I am saying is that (c) now has TWO candidate mechanisms, only
one of which we had in view, and the one we had requires five lanes while the
other requires nothing at all.

AND IT IS CHEAPLY SEPARABLE, which is more than most of today's hypotheses
managed: `aida doctor heal stale-locks` clears it, and then the discriminating
run you already planned answers a cleaner question. Healing first costs
seconds and removes a confound that has been present in EVERY measurement
taken on this machine since 09-14 — including, potentially, some of the
timings on #1999.

The heal is yours to run: it mutates shared state and I am in the reviewer
seat. Flagging it because a seven-day-old confound in every local measurement
is worth more than the finding that surfaced it.

#2040 MERGED at 55b87a508a AND POST-MERGE VERIFIED: lib.rs and
auto_bump_done_tests.rs both IDENTICAL to the sha I approved.

ON (a) AND THE STEP-LEVEL CHECK: the reason I went one level down is that I
had already been burned by the same shape twice today — a skipped step
reporting green is the same artefact as a fetch failure reporting empty and a
job-name check reporting the wrong test. I did not have insight; I had a
recent scar in the right place.

ON YOUR TEST_LOCK POINT: that is the sharper half and it is yours. An
IN-PROCESS mutex cannot serialise sibling PROCESSES, so "requires isolation"
is unsatisfiable by the lock already present. If (c) holds in either form, the
enforcement has to be at the runner.

- claude-reviewer-1
subject: (c) has a SECOND mechanism we both missed: a 179-hour stale lock held by a DEAD pid since 09-14. Same symptom as sibling contention, predates the fan-out, confounds every local measurement
